name: FAA 14 CFR Part 117 (flightcrew duty) + DOT 14 CFR Part 260 (passenger refunds)
applies_to: The US demo dataset (BTS 2025). US Part 121 carriers operate under 14 CFR Part 117, not DGCA.

primary_sources.document: 14 CFR Part 117 - Flight and Duty Limitations and Rest Requirements: Flightcrew Members
primary_sources.retrieved_via: eCFR versioner API, https://www.ecfr.gov/api/versioner/v1/full/2026-10-13/title-14.xml?part=117 (eCFR text up to date as of 2026-10-13)

primary_sources.document: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for Airline Fare and Ancillary Service Fees

report_buffer_minutes.source: 14 CFR 117.3: 'Report time means the time that the certificate holder requires a flightcrew member to report for an assignment.'
report_buffer_minutes.notes: Verified that Part 117 does NOT fix a report buffer - it is carrier-defined. 60 minutes is therefore an ASSUMPTION, not a regulatory number.

post_flight_buffer_minutes.source: 14 CFR 117.3: an FDP 'ends when the aircraft is parked after the last flight'. Post-flight duties are 'duty' (117.3 'Duty'), not FDP.
post_flight_buffer_minutes.notes: Because the FDP ends at block-in, this buffer is NOT added to the FDP compared against Table B. It only moves the release-from-duty time from which rest (117.25(e)) is measured. 15 minutes is an assumption.

standby_callout_minutes.source: None. Reserve response times are set in each carrier's reserve scheme.
standby_callout_minutes.notes: Lead time a standby crew needs between call-out and report. Used only to compute the action deadline. Assumption.

acclimated.notes: Crew assumed acclimated to the first departure airport's time zone, so the 117.13(b)(1) 30-minute reduction for non-acclimated crew is not applied.

rules.description: Maximum flight duty period, unaugmented two-pilot operation, from Table B: depends on the scheduled time of start (acclimated local time) and the number of flight segments.

threshold.column_basis: number of flight segments (7 means 7 or more)
threshold.row_basis: scheduled time of start, acclimated local time (HHMM, inclusive ranges)

rules.source: 14 CFR 117.13(a) and Table B to Part 117 - Flight Duty Period: Unaugmented Operations. https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-G/part-117
rules.notes: Table encoded verbatim (lineholder values). 117.13(a): no assignment if the scheduled FDP 'will exceed' the limit, so an FDP exactly at the limit is legal (comparator gt). Not modelled: 117.15 split duty, 117.17 augmented crews, 117.21 reserve-specific limits, non-acclimated reduction.

rules.description: Table B limit plus the maximum pre-takeoff extension. Beyond this the pilot in command and certificate holder cannot extend: the crew cannot legally start the leg.
rules.source: 14 CFR 117.19(a)(1): 'the pilot in command and the certificate holder may extend the maximum flight duty period permitted in Tables B or C of this part up to 2 hours.' https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-G/part-117
rules.notes: Extension applies only to unforeseen operational circumstances arising before takeoff; an extension of more than 30 min may occur only once before a 117.25(b) rest (117.19(a)(2)) and must be reported to the FAA within 10 days (117.19(a)(4)). 117.19(b) post-takeoff extensions (to land at the destination) are not modelled - this engine plans before takeoff. Cumulative-limit interaction (117.19(a)(3), 117.23(c)) not modelled: no crew history.

rules.description: Maximum flight time, unaugmented operation, by time of report (Table A).
rules.source: 14 CFR 117.11(a)(1) and Table A to Part 117 - Maximum Flight Time Limits for Unaugmented Operations. https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-G/part-117
rules.notes: Evaluated against SCHEDULED block time only (BTS CRS_ELAPSED_TIME). Delays in this model change departure/arrival times, not block time, so this rule is used to test whether the single-crew proxy is plausible for a rotation, never to raise a delay alert.

rules.description: Minimum rest of 10 consecutive hours before the next flight duty period, measured from release from duty.
rules.source: 14 CFR 117.25(e): 'a rest period of at least 10 consecutive hours immediately before beginning the reserve or flight duty period measured from the time the flightcrew member is released from duty.' https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-G/part-117
rules.notes: Evaluated only when the same aircraft operates on the next calendar date in the dataset (proxy: same crew). Rest = next day's report time - (projected block-in + post-flight buffer). The 8-hour uninterrupted sleep opportunity inside the 10 hours (117.25(e)) and 117.25(b) 30 h in 168 h are not modelled.

rules.description: 'Significantly delayed' domestic flight: scheduled to arrive 3 hours or more after the original scheduled arrival. A passenger who declines the delayed flight is entitled to a refund.
rules.source: 14 CFR 260.2, definition 'Significantly delayed or changed flight', paragraph (2): 'The consumer is scheduled to arrive at the destination airport three or more hours for domestic itineraries ... after the original scheduled arrival time'. https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-II/subchapter-A/part-260
rules.notes: Issued by DOT (not FAA) - included because the US profile otherwise has no passenger rule. All flights in the dataset are treated as domestic itineraries (6-hour international threshold not used). Predicted arrival delay = predicted departure delay x Layer 4 recovery rate. Applies to the passenger's itinerary; evaluated per flight here.

not_encoded.rule: 14 CFR 117.23 cumulative FDP / flight-time limits (60 h/168 h, 190 h/672 h, 100 h/672 h)
not_encoded.reason: Requires individual crew history; crew rosters are not public.

not_encoded.rule: 14 CFR 117.25(b) 30 consecutive hours free from duty in any 168 hours
not_encoded.reason: Requires a week of crew history.

not_encoded.rule: 14 CFR 117.15 split duty, 117.17 augmented operations (Table C), 117.21 reserve status
not_encoded.reason: Not observable from schedule data; demo assumes unaugmented lineholder crews.

not_encoded.rule: 14 CFR 259.4 tarmac delay (3 h domestic deplaning, food and water within 2 h)
not_encoded.reason: Verified in primary text but not applicable: the model predicts gate departure delay, not time on the tarmac with passengers boarded.

not_encoded.rule: US federal requirement to provide meals or hotels for gate delays
not_encoded.reason: Not found in the primary text reviewed (14 CFR 259.4 and Part 260). Part 259 was not reviewed in full. Carrier meal/hotel commitments are carrier-specific, so none is encoded.
